Bug_Title: RV: Bad attempt to compute absolute value of signed random integer (RV_ABSOLUTE_VALUE_OF_RANDOM_INT)
Bug_Details:
This code generates a random signed integer and then computes
the absolute value of that random integer.  If the number returned by the random number
generator is Integer.MIN_VALUE, then the result will be negative as well (since
Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE). (Same problem arises for long values as well).
 Integer.MIN_VALUE Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by using Math.abs() on a randomly generated integer. If the random integer happens to be Integer.MIN_VALUE, Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) will still return Integer.MIN_VALUE, which is incorrect since the absolute value should be positive.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method multiple times. Since the random number generator can produce Integer.MIN_VALUE, the Math.abs() function will return Integer.MIN_VALUE, which is negative. The assertions in the test cases check if the absolute value is non-negative, causing the test to fail when Integer.MIN_VALUE is encountered.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results indicate that both tests passed without any failures. Since the bug would cause the assertion to fail when the random integer generated is Integer.MIN_VALUE, and the tests did not fail, it suggests that Integer.MIN_VALUE was not generated during the test runs. Therefore, the test results do not confirm the presence of the bug.
